Parcel helps independent consultants organize client requests by project, track due dates, and export CSV files. It runs locally.

To get started, create a project and import a CSV of your client requests. Use the project view to review requests and their due dates, then export a CSV when you need a copy.
The scheduler can prepare your weekly report on Mondays, but you’ll need to approve each report before it sends. Unattended sending isn’t available.

Consistent file names help you find the right document quickly and make it easier for coworkers to understand what a file contains without opening it. A shared pattern also helps distinguish projects, dates, and versions, reducing the chance of using an outdated copy. For example, use “2026-10-24_Acme_Meeting-Notes_v01.docx” instead of “notes-final-new.docx.” Putting the date first in year-month-day order keeps files sorted chronologically. Agree on a simple naming pattern with your team, use clear project names, and update version numbers consistently. Keep names descriptive enough to recognize at a glance without making them unnecessarily long.
Fixed the search filter and opened [PR #12](https://example.com/pr/12) for your review and merge. All 18 targeted tests passed; CI is still running. Nothing has been deployed.

Choose a PDF to get a summary with links to the source pages. Scanned PDFs aren’t supported.
